method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, formula/macro/reference comparison, reverse paraphrase and bounded primary-source terminology research; not independent or human review.
scope: All ten translated blocks in Dedekind Algebras and Arithmetical Induction.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Any Dedekind algebra can stand in for the naturals because if X contains o and is successor-closed on N∩X, then minimality of N as the closure of o gives N⊆X. Thus a Dedekind-infinite set supplies a surrogate natural-number structure.
samples.checks: The theorem's restricted quantifier, implication proof, closure formula, subset conclusion and dependence on the earlier existence theorem are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The set-theoretic induction theorem yields the familiar formula schema, even when phi has parameters. Parameters are explained as arbitrary objects c1 through ck, and the fully universally closed formula displays every free variable.
samples.checks: The corollary label, set abstraction, all parameter variables, both ellipses, three aligned formula rows and later-part reference have exact parity.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Recursive definition will later justify addition, multiplication and exponentiation on any Dedekind algebra. The six displayed base and successor equations are stipulated and will be shown to have the expected behavior.
samples.checks: The delayed-justification qualification, chapter reference, Potter page citation and every recursive equation are unchanged. The established पुनरावर्ती variant is kept consistent while MR-P060 records the official प्रत्यावर्ती alternative.

limitations: No independent linguistic or mathematical review has been performed.
